Seth Godin's great book Purple Cow can give you inspiration in this department. Property hacks – You can use your creativity and knowledge to improve your profits with real estate investing. For example, you may decide to install tile or other hard surface floors in your rental. It may cost you 20% more now, but it saves you MANY times the cost over the next ten years of ownership. There are many other property hacks like this that give you an advantage.
I'm willing to bet you can find even more trade secrets to make yourself more competitive in real estate investing. That's the beauty of owning investments that you can personally impact.
Become a builder of moats
Warren Buffett has made billions of dollars for a reason. He invests with solid principles, like buying businesses with economic moats. He's also extremely smart, and he surrounds himself with other smart people like his partner Charlie Munger.
And as a Buffett nerd, I've tried to inspire you to model his success. But you don't have to copy him exactly. Instead, you can model his principles and apply them to real estate investing. It's an investment arena that allows you to create and protect your own investing success.
I wish you all the best with your own investing adventures!
summary: Learn how to get the competitive advantage in real estate investing.

title: Eskimos winners in last playoff game vs. Stampeders
text:
And, just like that, the tables have turned in the CFL’s Battle of Alberta.
Sure, the Calgary Stampeders have owned the provincial rivalry, sweeping the past 11-straight games against the Edmonton Eskimos.
But that was the regular season, and this is playoffs, meaning when the Eskimos take to McMahon Stadium for Sunday’s West Division final (2:30 p.m., TSN, 630 CHED), they will be the ones looking to ride out with a winning streak.
Edmonton currently has a one-game playoff advantage after defeating Calgary 33-19 in the 2011 West Division semifinal the last time the two teams met in the post-season.
Unfortunately for the Eskimos, it also counts as the last time they earned a victory over the Stampeders. Period.
So take it for what it’s worth. Just remember: there is a reason playoff statistics are kept separate from the rest.
And it sure means something to the veterans in their locker-room.
“It’s definitely not a small deal,” said slotback Fred Stamps, who, along with fullback Calvin McCarty, are the two longest-serving Eskimos winding up their eighth season with the only CFL club they’ve ever belonged to. “We’re going against a team that beat us three times this year. That’s the only team we haven’t beat.
“Our team right now, we’re playing real focused football: Special teams is making plays, defence is making plays, offence controlling the ball. So we’ve just got to carry that over and prepare.”
And this week, it’s only the ‘right now,’ that matters to the Eskimos.
After all, you wouldn’t need more than two hands to count the current names on the roster who were with the team for the end of that 2011 season.
Fred Stamps, Calvin McCarty, Adarius Bowman, Nate Coehoorn. Mike Miller. Matt Nichols, Brian Ramsay, Corbin Sharun and J.C. Sherritt. Defensive tackle Almondo Sewell started the year out, but was released one-third of the way through.
That makes it 9 1/3, at best, of the current Eskimos active 46-man roster who have known anything other than losing to Calgary.
Then again, with 21 players on that list in their first (or, in two cases, first in a long time) season in Edmonton, if not the CFL, a 12-win season here is the only thing they know.
Still, none of those have come against Calgary, and Stamps and the rest of the veteran-leadership group can’t stress enough upon the fresh faces not to take this situation for granted.
Edmonton will only have made it to the divisional final three times in the past nine seasons since their last Grey Cup (2008, 2011 and 2014).
“Right now, I’m doing whatever it takes to help the team win,” said Stamps, who has seen a significant if not utterly disappointing drop in playing time down the playoff stretch. “Talking to the guys on the sideline, try to keep them in the game and stuff like that.
“I’m pretty sure they understand how big this game is now, so it’s really exciting and I just can’t wait. Man, it feels good. Let’s put it like that.”
While Stamps finished second on the team with 545 yards and two touchdowns — his lowest totals since his rookie season back in 2007 — he watched teammate Adarius Bowman take over the receiving spotlight by leading the league in receiving yards.
And despite missing out on a 1,000-yard season for the first time since 2008, Stamps’s only focus is on the team getting back to that 2011 form.
“We’re having a similar year,” he said of the squad that went 11-7 on the way to a West Division final appearance against the eventual Grey Cup champion B.C. Lions. “We’ve just got to finish it off this week.”
Besides, offence isn’t necessarily what Stamps credits this year’s success to.
“When you take the field as a team and you have confidence in knowing your defence is going to get the ball back to you, what more could you ask for?” he said of what was the league’s leading defence, both in yards and points allowed. “That’s the true definition of defence wins championships.”
ESKS TRIO GRAB AWARDS
It’s the latest candidate for 2014’s Most CFL Thing Ever award: the Edmonton Eskimos defence leads the way to an 18-10 win over the Saskatchewan Roughriders with six interceptions in last week’s West Division semifinal and, wouldn’t you know it, that’s the only weekly award they didn’t win.
Instead, the defensive player of the week was Montreal Alouettes defensive back Jerald Brown, who had five tackles, and interception, a knockdown, a fumble recovery and a touchdown in a 50-17 win over the B.C. Lions.
Offensive honours went to Edmonton running back John White, who ran for 134 yards on 19 carries, as well as two catches for 14 yards.
“It just comes down to who wants it more,” White said of the way the ground game gets focused on in the frigid playoff setting. “I did a lot of hitting out there (Sunday), not too many moves, but that’s what coach (Chris) Jones wanted, so that’s what I gave him.”
Special-teamer Kendial Lawrence was singled out for his 84-yard punt-return touchdown that stood as Edmonton’s lone visit to the end zone last Sunday, while defensive tackle Gregory Alexandre was named the Canadian player of the week for his two sacks and two tackles in the win.
